data.q: What data does the platform serve?
data.a: {provider}'s quarterly KPI estimates for public companies: completed-quarter (historical) estimates and quarter-to-date snapshots that update at most daily.

answer.q: How is a chat answer produced?
answer.a: A language model calls four read-only MCP tools (search companies, list KPIs, get history, get QTD). Every call, with its arguments and result, is shown next to the answer and stored in an audit table.

typo.q: What happens when I misspell a company or KPI?
typo.a: The tool returns a structured error with the closest matches and a hint. The assistant retries once with the suggestion and tells you what it did.

clients.q: Can I use it from Claude Desktop or Cursor?
clients.a: Yes. The MCP server runs over stdio for desktop clients and over HTTP for services. The developer page has the exact configuration.

noKey.q: Does it work without an LLM API key?
noKey.a: Yes. A deterministic stub provider runs the same tool-calling flow, so the demo, tests and CI never need a key. Set a key to use a real model.

database.q: How do you keep the model away from the database?
database.a: The model only sees tool schemas and results. Tools go through one domain layer with parameterised queries; identity comes from the server, never from the model.

tenancy.a: It is multi-tenant-ready: every call carries a tenant id and the audit trail records it. Row-level security is the documented next step.

selfHost.a: One command starts Postgres, the API, the MCP server, the chat app and this site with Docker Compose. Each part also ships as its own image and can be deployed on its own.

platform.title: One domain layer, three protocol surfaces
platform.subtitle: REST, MCP and the chat agent are thin adapters over the same services, so validation, suggestions and error semantics are defined once.

security.title: Boundaries between the model and the data
security.subtitle: No login is needed for the demo, so the design focuses on the boundaries that matter for an agent platform.

llm.title: LLM ↔ tools
llm.text: The model receives tool schemas and tool results only. Arguments it produces are sanitised twice: in the agent and in the MCP server.

data.title: Tools ↔ data
data.text: Tools call one domain layer that uses parameterised ORM queries. A CI gate fails the build if raw SQL appears outside migrations.

callers.title: Callers ↔ services
callers.text: Per-client rate limits, request body caps, CORS allowlists, health checks and non-root containers.

failures.title: Each failure mode has a guard and a test

hallucination.guard: Error envelope with suggestions and a recovery hint; the prompt allows one retry.

unknownTool.guard: Rejected in the agent before any network call; the model is told which tools exist.

malformed.guard: Never executed; recorded as a rejected step.

identity.guard: No such parameter exists; unknown keys are dropped and counted.

loop.guard: Iteration budget, duplicate-failing-call ledger and a wall-clock limit.

slow.guard: Per-call timeouts and result truncation with a note to the model.

outage.guard: Explained to the user; partial steps are persisted with the trace id.
